findings.desc: scope_extension_proposal does not persist the proposal body when a separate reason is supplied. The CLI schema asks for proposal plus optional reason, and ScopeExtensionProposal has proposal/proposalTextHash fields for the human-readable expansion proposal, but the handler calls buildScopeExtensionProposal with only reason: args.reason || args.proposal and patch: {}, so args.proposal is discarded whenever reason is present (packages/main/src/handlers/scope-anti-expansion.ts:246). The builder used by the handler never writes proposal/proposalTextHash (packages/main/src/core/scope-anti-expansion.ts:656), while the typed artifact builder below does preserve them (packages/main/src/core/scope-anti-expansion.ts:960). This means the gate-consumed scope-extension-proposals.json can block INIT_CHECK but not reliably record what expansion was proposed, undermining the proposal/discard/decision audit flow required for INIT reviewers to propose rather than mutate scope.

The INIT scope anti-expansion gate can be satisfied with empty boundary artifacts. Evidence: cli-engine.ts:501-520 declares scope_boundary_set.allowedScope as an array without min(1), and execution_boundary_set has all boundary fields optional. handlers/scope-anti-expansion.ts:183-215 writes scope/execution artifacts without requiring any allowed/excluded scope term or command/tool policy; this differs from story-create.ts:466-472, which does require a non-empty initial allowed scope. core/scope-anti-expansion.ts:532-616 evaluates existing empty artifacts as a pass when no keyword/repeat issues exist, and machine.ts:189-225 then only checks stored pass/hash/freshness. A caller can save empty scope/execution boundaries, run scope_freeze_check, and satisfy the scope gate with no effective user-confirmed boundary.

story_create can create INIT_CHECK stories that cannot satisfy or repair the new scope gate. Evidence: the fromDraft branch writes the new story directly with phase INIT_CHECK and deletes the draft without writing scope-boundary.json, execution-boundary.json, or scope-freeze-check.json (handlers/story-create.ts:247-351). The CLI then calls dev_start directly for that result (cli-engine.ts:3819-3829). dev_start now rejects INIT_CHECK/no-worktree stories when getScopeAntiExpansionGuardFailureReason reports missing scope artifacts (handlers/worktree.ts:632-638). The only commands that can create or refresh those artifacts are INIT-only by handler and policy (handlers/scope-anti-expansion.ts:74-79; core/command-policy.ts:287-291), so fromDraft leaves the story stuck in INIT_CHECK with no normal CLI repair path. The direct story_create phase=INIT_CHECK path has the same shape: it can write scope/execution artifacts but never writes a freeze check, and scope_freeze_check is no longer callable after phase INIT_CHECK.
